subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: On which day of the week is Shabbat observed?
questions.explain: Shabbat is the seventh day, Saturday, kept holy as the day of rest.

questions.q: At approximately what time does Shabbat begin each week?
questions.explain: Shabbat begins at sunset on Friday and ends after nightfall on Saturday when three stars appear.

questions.q: What is the name of the ceremony that marks the end of Shabbat?
questions.explain: Havdalah, using a candle, wine and spices, separates Shabbat from the ordinary week.

questions.q: Why are two loaves of challah placed on the Shabbat table?
options: To represent the two tablets of stone
To recall the double portion of manna given before Shabbat
questions.explain: The two loaves recall the double portion of manna God provided on Fridays in the wilderness.

questions.q: Which event in the Torah does the Shabbat rest primarily commemorate?
options: God resting on the seventh day after creation
The giving of the Torah at Sinai
The crossing of the Red Sea
questions.explain: Genesis describes God resting on the seventh day, which Jews imitate by resting on Shabbat.

questions.q: Refraining from work on Shabbat is directly commanded by which of the Ten Commandments?
options: Remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy
questions.explain: The fourth commandment instructs Jews to keep the Sabbath day holy by resting.

questions.q: In which Hebrew month do Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur fall?
questions.explain: Rosh Hashanah begins on 1 Tishrei and Yom Kippur follows on 10 Tishrei.

questions.q: Which instrument is traditionally sounded during Rosh Hashanah services?
questions.explain: The shofar, a ram's horn, is blown to call worshippers to repentance at Rosh Hashanah.

questions.q: By what English name is Yom Kippur also known?
questions.explain: Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement, is the holiest day when Jews seek forgiveness for their sins.

questions.q: What is the opening prayer of the Yom Kippur evening service called?
questions.explain: Kol Nidre is chanted at the start of Yom Kippur, annulling unfulfilled vows made to God.

questions.q: Why are apples dipped in honey at Rosh Hashanah?
options: To recall the plague of locusts
To express hope for a sweet new year
To represent the fruit of the Temple
To symbolise the bitterness of exile
questions.explain: The sweet apple and honey express the wish for a good and sweet year ahead.

questions.q: What is the main religious observance of Yom Kippur?
questions.explain: Jews fast for around 25 hours and spend the day in prayer seeking God's forgiveness.

questions.q: What is the significance of the period between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur?
options: A time of feasting and celebration
The Ten Days of Repentance, a time to seek forgiveness
A period of mourning for the Temple
The counting of the harvest weeks
questions.explain: These Ten Days of Repentance (Days of Awe) are for reflection, teshuvah and putting wrongs right.

questions.q: Which event does Pesach (Passover) commemorate?
options: The giving of the Torah at Sinai
The Exodus of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt
questions.explain: Pesach recalls God freeing the Israelites from slavery and their escape from Egypt.

questions.q: What type of bread is eaten during Pesach?
questions.explain: Only unleavened matzah is eaten during Pesach, as all leaven (chametz) is removed.

questions.q: What is the name of the special meal held on the first night(s) of Pesach?
questions.explain: The Seder is an ordered ritual meal at which the Exodus story is retold from the Haggadah.

questions.q: Why is only unleavened bread eaten during Pesach?
options: To recall that the Israelites left Egypt in haste with no time for bread to rise
To symbolise the sweetness of freedom
Because bread was forbidden in the wilderness
To represent the manna from heaven
questions.explain: The Israelites fled so quickly their dough had no time to rise, so matzah recalls that haste.

questions.q: On the Seder plate, what do the bitter herbs (maror) symbolise?
options: The mortar used by the slaves
The bitterness of slavery in Egypt
The tears of joy at freedom
questions.explain: Maror, usually horseradish, represents the bitter suffering of the Israelites under slavery.

questions.q: A family lights two candles at sunset on Friday, recites a blessing over wine and shares two plaited loaves before resting from work. Which observance is this?
questions.explain: Candles, Kiddush over wine and two challot at Friday sunset are the hallmarks of welcoming Shabbat.

questions.q: A person abstains from food and drink for around 25 hours, wears no leather shoes and attends the Kol Nidre service. Which day is being observed?
questions.explain: Fasting, avoiding leather footwear and the Kol Nidre prayer are all central to Yom Kippur.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Religious Studies (0490) syllabus; Judaism: Festivals & Fasts
